name: CDMG (chemically defined medium CDM + 2% glucose), agar plate (PMC12816087)
description: CDMG (chemically defined medium CDM + 2% glucose), agar plate — medium reported in PMC12816087 (complex/undefined base — extracts not BiGG-mappable).

provenance.citation: Medium composition from PMC12816087 (see GrowthDB record).
provenance.notes: Full recipe recovered from the primary literature: base medium 'CDM35 (chemically defined medium, 35 components; final pH 7). Target medium CDMG = CDM35 base with glucose at 2% (20 g/L). CDMG agar plate additionally contains agar + an acidic chromogenic agent (pH indicator) used to detect acid production.' (Ponomarova O., Gabrielli N., Sevin D.C., Mulleder M., Zirngibl K., Bulyha K., Andrejev S., Kafkia E., Typas A., Sauer U., Ralser M., Patil K.R. 'Yeast creates a niche for symbiotic lactic aci
provenance.verification_evidence: CDMG liquid medium was 2% glucose added to CDM liquid medium ... CDMG or CDMS agar plates were prepared in the same way as MRS agar plates, except that CDMG or CDMS liquid medium was mixed with 1.0% (w/v) agar
provenance.recipe_evidence: Target paper (Liao et al., PMC12816087, Methods): 'CDM liquid medium was made as described by Olga et al.[49]' and 'CDMG liquid medium was 2% glucose added to CDM liquid medium'; CDMG agar plates 'containing 2% glucose (CDMG)' with an acidic chromogenic agent, incubated at 30 C. Base recipe from reference [49] = Ponomarova et al. 2017 Cell Systems, Table S1 'CDM35 medium composition (final pH 7)': Carbon Source Glucose 15 g/L; Amino Acids L-Arginine 0.72, L-Asparagine 0.5, L-Histidine 0.17, L-Isoleucine 0.24, L-Leucine 1, L-Methionine 0.125, L-Tyrosine 0.3, L-Valine 0.7; Vitamins Biotin 0.006,
provenance.base_medium: CDM35 (chemically defined medium, 35 components; final pH 7). Target medium CDMG = CDM35 base with glucose at 2% (20 g/L). CDMG agar plate additionally contains agar + an acidic chromogenic agent (pH indicator) used to detect acid production.
provenance.base_medium_reference: Ponomarova O., Gabrielli N., Sevin D.C., Mulleder M., Zirngibl K., Bulyha K., Andrejev S., Kafkia E., Typas A., Sauer U., Ralser M., Patil K.R. 'Yeast creates a niche for symbiotic lactic acid bacteria through nitrogen overflow.' Cell Systems 5(4):345-357.e6 (2017). DOI 10.1016/j.cels.2017.09.002; PMID 28964698; PMC5660601. Full CDM35 composition given in Supplemental Table S1 (mmc1). This is reference [49] ('Olga et al.') cited by the target paper.
